benchmark.name: PDB post-cutoff single chains
benchmark.cutoff_source: Lin et al., bioRxiv 2022.07.20.500902, 'Structure training sets for ESMFold'
benchmark.selection: RCSB search: exptl.method=X-RAY DIFFRACTION, deposited chains 1-3, entity length 40-500. NO date constraint -- the cutoff is applied by benchmark.select so the filter the held-out claim rests on is exercised on real entries rather than pre-satisfied by the query.
limitations: Every post-cutoff entry in the sampled pool fell in a single 2026 window; RCSB's default result ordering returned a bimodal sample (1976-1999 and 2026, nothing between). The set is therefore ~6 years past the training cutoff -- conservative for leakage -- but spans only about six months of depositions, so it is narrower in time than a benchmark drawn across 2020-2026 would be.

No homology screen was run against pre-cutoff structures. A post-cutoff entry can be a point mutant or close homolog of a structure ESMFold trained on, so the date filter bounds memorisation of that exact entry, not generalisation.

n_chains is deposited_polymer_entity_instance_count, pinned against a live RCSB response (1UBQ reports 1). This is the deposited chain count, which is what the runner's single-protein-chain guard checks.

applicability_domain.notes: single chains only; measured on this benchmark set
